title: Halfbeat reset pattern correlation - lab notes and suggested runbook
content:
Summary:

This doc is a working lab journal for a set of intermittent node resets we observed across a small subset of racks during the 2028-08-14 -> 2028-08-17 window. Pattern: short hard resets (~10-30s) that leave the host kernel and hypervisor intact but drop all GPU devices for a brief epoch and then recover. These do not match historical full-power-cycling ghost resets; they are fast and often correlate with a very short ECC correctable-error burst or a single NV fabric retrain in syslogs. Purpose: capture observations, narrow hypotheses, and propose a lightweight runbook we can trial on canary nodes.

Observed symptom cluster (applied to 7 nodes across 3 racks):
- Short device disappearance from /dev and nvidia-smi showing transient NVML timeouts.
- Kernel dmesg reports: pci-e AER correctable error logs followed by GPU driver returning -ENXIO on several contexts, then device re-probed.
- On affected nodes, hwmon shows a sub-1s negative voltage dip on one PMIC rail (~0.1-0.3V) in telemetry at the same timestamp as the reset (observed in BMC sensor spike logs).
- No BMC watchdog power-cycle; BMC logs show the host remained responsive over IPMI.
- When a node recovers the GPU, ECC counts often show a small clustered increase in correctable ECC counters for a single memory bank.
- Frequency: 1–5 events per day across the fleet slice.

Data capture we used:
- preflight-capture template applied on 3 canary nodes (capture-id: halfbeat-2028-08-16-01). Collected: full dmesg, journalctl -b -1, nvml logs (NVML trace level 3), BMC sensor dump (last 2000 entries), PMIC logging windowed slice, sysfs GPU diag counters, and live tcpdump on host-to-gpu-fabric-control channels.
- Short timeline extract for node r12-n3 (iso timestamps):
  - 2028-08-16T03:14:11.421Z: PMIC rail Vcc_gpu dips -0.18V for 420ms (BMC sensor sample).
  - 2028-08-16T03:14:11.845Z: pci_e AER correctable error: Data link protocol error on port X (slot 3).
  - 2028-08-16T03:14:12.103Z: NVIDIA driver: pcie link down for GPU0, nvml reports ENXIO on handle fetch.
  - 2028-08-16T03:14:12.912Z: kernel: device re-probed, nvml reconnect, ECC corrected counter +7 on membank 2.

Immediate hypotheses (ranked):
1) Local power microtransient hitting GPU PMIC/regulator causing short PCIe link flaps. Explains negative voltage dip and timing.
2) NVLink/link training sensitivity combined with a driver-side timeout path (driver aggressively detaches on certain AER patterns).
3) Early-stage firmware regression in GPU vBIOS that mishandles a particular AER code combination and triggers an internal reset (less likely given hardware vendor FW notes).
4) Intermittent DIMM bitstorms in a particular bank manifest as ECC bursts and trigger link degrades (possible but ECC bursts are very small).

What we tried so far (experiments and outcomes):
- Increased AER threshold in kernel module parameters on one canary node (aer_inject throttling): reduced visible kernel AER logs for sustained noise but did not prevent device disappearance. Outcome: marginal improvement in log noise but not reliable.
- Forced nvlink retrain suppression (patched driver knob to increase link training retries): on patched canary, we saw one event still but with longer re-probe time. Outcome: increased recovery time, not eliminated.
- Power rail clamp test: swapped PMIC daughterboard between nodes (r12-n3 and r18-n1). Events moved with PMICboard -> supports PMIC/reg board hypothesis.
- Firmware review with vendor: vendor noted an older nvlink microcode variant on affected inventory. They released a microcode update flagged as 'stability for link training under noisy rails'. We scheduled staged rollout on 3 nodes. After update, two nodes had zero events in 72h window; one node still had transient.

Non-invasive mitigations for production while root cause is pinned:
- Route critical latency-sensitive workloads away from nodes that show >1 event/week (automated via node labelling).
- Enable autoprobing fallback to synthetic model shard for jobs (avoid hard failures due to ENXIO in production agent).
- Add short auto-throttle in our scheduler: when node sees a transient NVML ENXIO, mark node as "soft-unavailable" for 30s to allow device re-probe before killing tasks.

Proposed lightweight runbook (can be executed by oncall SRE):
1) Preliminary triage (first 10 minutes):
   - Check current alerts: gpu-reset spikes (grafana panel), scheduled maintenance windows.
   - ssh to node, gather logs: /var/log/dmesg, journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -S -5m, ipmitool sensor list > /tmp/bmc-sensors.txt, nvml-snapshot tool (attached). Upload artifacts to the incident thread.
   - If BMC sensor shows >0.1V drop on Vcc_gpu window, escalate to hardware team and tag the node for PMIC reseat.
2) Containment (10-30 minutes):
   - Label node in k8s as gpu:unstable to prevent new pods from scheduling: kubectl label node <n> gpu-status=unstable --overwrite.
   - Apply soft-unavailable via autoscaler to signal control plane to avoid scheduling.
3) Short remediation (30-90 minutes):
   - Re-seat GPU riser and PMIC daughterboard (if in colo/on prem and safe). Steps documented in rack hardware playbook (link in linked_artifacts).
   - If re-seat not possible, power-cycle GPU only via vendor utility (avoid full host power-cycle).
4) Post-remediation verification (90-180 minutes):
   - Run stress profile: 10 minutes of memory-bound kernel on GPU (our memtest workload), monitor ECC counters and BMC sensors.
   - If no repeat in 3 hours, remove labels and place node into a monitored canary pool for 72 hours.
5) Escalation (if repeats after remediation):
   - Open P1 with vendor support including full preflight capture id, BMC dump and PMIC telemetry. Request hardware replacement (PMIC/reg board) under warranty.

Metrics and dashboards to add (short list):
- 1m spike panel for NVML ENXIO errors per node with zoom-to-logs link.
- PMIC rail short-dip histogram windowed by 1h to detect microtransient frequency.
- Node "soft-unavailable" churn and correlation with reset events.

Open questions & followups:
- Are any jobs skewed to memory bank 2 (where ECC increments were observed)? Need to correlate model shards with physical bank mapping (ask platform team).
- Can we instrument a higher sample-rate PMIC telemetry for a 24h period on a suspect node (risk: higher BMC load)?
- Do vendor microcode fixes fully eliminate event on broad inventory? Plan: schedule progressive rollout and capture SLA regression checks.

Notes to hardware team: when you swap PMIC boards, capture serial numbers and attach to ticket JIRA-OPS-4127. If replacement reduces events to zero across 7 days, mark root cause likely PMIC/regulator aging.

Appendix: common quick commands (copyable):
- ipmitool sdr elist | egrep -i "VCC_GPU|PMIC|VRM" > /tmp/bmc-sensors.txt
- journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -b -n 500 > /tmp/nv-driver.log
- nvml-snapshot --level 3 --output /tmp/nvml.json
- sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-tail.txt
- sudo cat /sys/devices/pci0000:00/0000:00:XX.X/eee/err_status

Contact: Lena Park (oncall SRE lead), slack:@lena.park.

Status of doc: working lab notes intended to be converted into a formal runbook once vendor replacement trial concludes. Please add comments inline or ping in slack thread linked in linked_artifacts.
